chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudaylah from Husayn from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm if a man prays by placing his knees on the ground before his hands." For it is understood to be in the state of necessity, and for one who cannot touch the ground with his hands first due to an ailment or illness.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to place knees before hands during prostration in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that placing the knees before the hands during prostration is permissible, specifically accommodating those with physical limitations or necessity. While the standard practice (sunnah) prioritizes placing the hands first, this ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (rukhas) in worship, ensuring that physical constraints do not invalidate the prayer's validity.
